newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FRAGILE CZECH CROWN HOLDS IN TIGHT RANGE.
newsitem.headline: FRAGILE CZECH CROWN HOLDS IN TIGHT RANGE.

text.p: The Czech crown continued an uneasy slumber on Wednesday as dealers awaited possible further fallout from the cabinet's political troubles and a renewed attack on the currency as short-term rates ease.
At 11.30 a.m. (0930 gmt) the crown had barely moved at 32.888 to the dollar and 18.978 mark from Tuesday levels at 32.991 and 19.100.

"What will have a quiet serious impact on the (foreign exchange market) would be the political situation. Next week there should be the confidence vote for the government... even during the voting the crown can be volatile," said Tomas Novak, chief trader at Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka.
Last week, downward pressure on the currency forced the Czech National Bank to float the crown allowing it to fall more than 10 percent against its former mark/dollar peg.
That was followed by an emergency package of austerity measures and a cabinet reshuffle which has come under fire in the media and from opposition politicians.

Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus has said he plans to ask the lower house of parliament, where his ruling coalition holds 100 of the 200 seats, for a vote of confidence in his government, probably next week.
"If (Klaus) doesn't get support from the parliament, we may see the Czech crown weaker," Novak said.
Some dealers have said the crown's equilibrium point is still another five to 10 percent lower than current levels, but has been kept in place by the illiquid market.
A two-tiered market has formed since the central bank has limited non-resident access to the money market where funds were being used for short-selling the crown.

The central bank has slightly eased its prohibitive short-term repo rates this week, draining two-week funds on Wednesday at 39 percent, after lowering one-week repo rates earlier this week to 45 percent from last week's 75 percent.
Traders expect further volatility as rates go lower and foreign investors are allowed back into the money market.
Despite the lowering of the repo rates, the Czech agency CTK quoted a central bank spokesman as saying on Wednesday that the CNB was not considering a change in its monetary policy.
